metadata.title: [TESTING]: Replace headless Chromium in Playwright e2e with Obscura for faster test runs" labels: testing, enhancement, triage
metadata.author: Lang-Akshay

description:
## Summary

`make test-ui-headless` and `make test-ui-headless-parallel` use headless Chromium via `pytest-playwright`, which is slow to start, memory-heavy, and adds significant wall-clock time to CI and local dev loops.

Replace the browser backend with [Obscura](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura) — a lightweight browser automation layer — to cut e2e test cycle time.

## Current Behaviour

```makefile
# Makefile (lines ~7438-7445)
playwright-install: uv
    @$(UV_BIN) run playwright install $(PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALL_FLAGS) chromium

test-ui-headless:
    # runs tests/playwright/ suite against headless Chromium

test-ui-headless-parallel:
    # same suite via pytest-xdist workers, each spawning a Chromium process
```

Problems:

- Chromium binary is ~300 MB; cold install blocks CI
- Each `pytest-xdist` worker spawns an independent Chromium process → high memory, slow parallelism
- Browser launch overhead dominates short tests (smoke, HTMX, CRUD)

## Proposed Change

Integrate [Obscura](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura) as the browser backend for the two headless make targets:

1. Add `obscura` as a dev dependency (or install via the existing `playwright-install` target)
2. Wire `conftest.py` `browser_type_launch_args` / `browser` fixture to use Obscura when `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER=obscura` env is set
3. Update `test-ui-headless` and `test-ui-headless-parallel` to set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER=obscura`
4. Keep `test-ui` (headed) and `test-ui-debug` on Chromium — Obscura is headless-only path

Makefile sketch:

```makefile
test-ui-headless: playwright-preflight
	PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER=obscura \
	$(UV_BIN) run pytest $(PLAYWRIGHT_DIR) --headless --tb=short $(PLAYWRIGHT_EXTRA_ARGS)

test-ui-headless-parallel: playwright-preflight
	PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER=obscura \
	$(UV_BIN) run pytest $(PLAYWRIGHT_DIR) --headless -n auto --tb=short $(PLAYWRIGHT_EXTRA_ARGS)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make test-ui-headless` completes faster than current Chromium baseline (measure with `time make test-ui-headless`)
- [ ] `make test-ui-headless-parallel` scales without per-worker Chromium memory spike
- [ ] All existing smoke markers (`smoke`, `ui`, `htmx`, `crud`) pass under Obscura
- [ ] `make test-ui` (headed/debug) still uses Chromium — no regression
- [ ] `playwright-install` target unchanged; Obscura install added as separate `obscura-install` target or folded into `playwright-preflight`
- [ ] CI workflow (`.github/workflows/`) updated to call `obscura-install` before headless test jobs

## Scope

- `Makefile` — `test-ui-headless`, `test-ui-headless-parallel`, `playwright-preflight`
- `tests/playwright/conftest.py` — browser fixture env-switch
- `.github/workflows/` — CI install step

## References

- Obscura: https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura
- Current install: `Makefile:7438` (`playwright-install`)
- Current headless targets: `Makefile:7400` (`.PHONY` list)
- Playwright conftest: `tests/playwright/conftest.py`

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: Reading Obscura's docs, it doesn't seem like a good replacement for Chromium as the main playwright browser. Although it's amazingly fast, it will not reflect the behaviour of a chrome-based browser, which is the main goal of the UI tests.
